baseline_facts.content: Cough began five to six days ago.
Cough keeps patient up at night.
Patient reports throat irritation from coughing.
Throat discomfort is not worse with swallowing.
No shortness of breath during routine activities.
Patient reports muscle pain in arms.
Patient reports muscle pain in legs.
Diarrhea started at the same time as the cough.
Increased water intake during diarrhea episode.
Fluid intake returned to normal after diarrhea resolved.
Patient takes Lisinopril for high blood pressure.
Patient regularly attends doctor check-ups for diabetes and high blood pressure.
Patient reports diabetes is under control with medication.
Patient reports blood pressure is under control with medication.
Partner has no symptoms of illness.
Patient stopped smoking six months ago.
Patient drinks alcohol no more than three evenings per week.
Patient drinks two to three glasses of wine per drinking evening.
Doctor advised drinking plenty of fluids.
Doctor advised to return if not improving in two to three days.
Doctor advised antibiotics may be considered if still feverish and cough not improving.
Doctor advised taking one to two days off work.
Doctor advised to seek care sooner if breathing worsens.
Doctor advised illness usually lasts about a week to ten days.
Doctor advised reducing alcohol consumption to two glasses per week initially.

candidate_facts.content: Dry, continuous cough started about 5–6 days ago.
Throat irritation from coughing is present.
Nighttime chills with shivering are reported.
Muscle aches are more pronounced in arms and legs.
Overall weakness or lethargy is reported.
Past medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Family history: Father has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Alcohol intake is wine, about 2–3 glasses on 3 evenings per week.
Diagnosis is acute viral upper respiratory infection.
Paracetamol (acetaminophen) recommended as needed for symptom relief.
Antibiotics were not started at this visit.
Antibiotics may be considered if not improving in 2–3 days.
Antibiotics may be considered if fever develops.
Antibiotics may be considered if persistent chest symptoms develop.
Re-evaluation recommended in 2–3 days if symptoms persist or worsen.
Seek earlier reassessment if fever develops.
Seek earlier reassessment if cough worsens.
Seek earlier reassessment if cough becomes productive.
Seek earlier reassessment if breathing worsens.
Advised to consider taking 1–2 days off work.
Return to work as symptoms allow.
Suggested goal is two glasses of alcohol per week initially.
Further reduction in alcohol may be considered if tolerated.
